subject: Review of the A′ proposal — what is accepted, what is corrected with evidence
reviewerProposal: A′ : preserve frozen v2/v5, adopt qualified production reachability as the new authority, produce a correction manifest + derived v6 lineage. B rejected as a final solution.
verdict: A′ is ACCEPTED as the right direction. Three of its details are corrected below; two of them change the target numbers.

accepted.point: B is not a final solution
accepted.why: read-model and production evidence already measured that 5 boundaries are recorded PROVEN although their only same-named production call sites are on unrelated types. Leaving the status as-is keeps a factually incorrect claim in the canonical audit.

accepted.point: frozen v2 need not be touched; add a lineage instead of overwriting history
accepted.why: v2 and v5 are historical artifacts under the pre-correction authority. Overwriting them would destroy the provenance that makes this audit reviewable.
accepted.addendum: The 112 relation corrections in v5 are not re-opened. A reachability correction only changes which boundaries carry coverage obligations; it does not invalidate any relation proof.

corrections.point: REVIEW_REQUIRED is NOT an admissible final status
corrections.evidence: scripts/ts6-phase-b-transaction-authority-validator.ts:826 raises the issue code PRODUCTION_REVIEW_REQUIRED for ANY boundary whose productionReachability.status === 'REVIEW_REQUIRED', and validateCorpus therefore returns valid=false. The schema defines the status (line 100) and buildAuditShape pins the classification bucket REVIEW_REQUIRED: 0 (line 649).
corrections.consequence: A snapshot containing a REVIEW_REQUIRED boundary can never pass the validator. 94 / 18 / 1 would be a snapshot the tool rejects.
corrections.correctReading: REVIEW_REQUIRED is the correct way to REPRESENT unresolved reachability, and the validator correctly treats its presence as a gate failure. It is not a state a final projection may ship in.

corrections.point: the inventory claim needs a precision: 120 / 113 / 11 / 87 survives, the SCOREBOARD does not
corrections.evidence: rawTransactionSites (11), boundaries (113), candidates (120) and historical rows (87) are counted independently of status, so they are unchanged. But corpus.summary.TX_BOUNDARY / TEST_ONLY_OR_DEAD / REVIEW_REQUIRED and candidateReconciliation[].c2r2Classification are DERIVED from status (scripts/ts6-phase-b-transaction-authority-validator.ts:584, 629, 646-649, 908-911).
corrections.consequence: The reviewer's statement that 120/113/11/87 cannot break is correct. The earlier phrasing in my own report ('invalidates the 120/113/11/87 invariant') was imprecise: what a status correction changes is the TX_BOUNDARY/TEST_ONLY_OR_DEAD split and the summary counts, which are re-derived, not part of the frozen inventory.

corrections.point: 94 / 18 / 1 is not what an authority can emit — it is a hand-triage result, and a different valid call site exists for the 1
evidence: Applying the qualified resolver mechanically to all 113 boundaries yields PROVEN 83 / TEST_ONLY_OR_DEAD 14 / REVIEW_REQUIRED 16 (measurement recorded in .qualified-classification.json).
The 94 figure came from adding 12 hand-traced recoveries to the resolver's 82. Those 12 fixes are not encoded in the resolver, so an automated authority cannot reproduce 94 today.

PostgresConnectorRuntimeState.recoverExpiredLeases does have a registered production call site: the constructor registers setInterval(() => { void this.recoverExpiredLeases(); }, 5_000) (adapters/connector-runtime-postgres/src/index.ts:1367). The resolver excludes it under the doctrine that a call in the boundary's own class is not external reachability.

The lifecycle is started in the canonical production path: package.json "start" -> assemblies/shotgun-app/src/main.ts -> startShotgunApplication -> application.ts:1207 passes new PostgresConnectorRuntimeState(pool) -> server.ts:2968 awaits options.connectorRuntimeState.lifecycle.start().
corrections.consequence: recoverExpiredLeases is neither a name collision nor an unresolvable receiver. It is a registered timer callback in the canonical production composition: genuinely reachable, but reachable from inside its own class, which the current reachability doctrine does not count. It remains a REVIEW_REQUIRED-class case, and therefore a TS-6 FINAL blocker — correctly identified as a blocker, but for a doctrinal reason rather than a configuration unknown.

authoritativeMeasurement.authority: qualified resolver — PROVEN iff a production call site's receiver statically resolves to the boundary class or to a Port the boundary implements
authoritativeMeasurement.note: The 5 confirmed collisions are the same five identified by hand triage. The 10 unresolved ones are the boundaries whose wiring was hand-traced successfully (sources product service via the process-global write runtime, semantic corpus reader through a structural inline parameter type, the command gateway through dependency objects, the connector runtime repository through an object-literal factory, the comparison repository through a module input member).

whatAdoptionRequires: Close REVIEW_REQUIRED to zero, else the projection is invalid by construction. Two ways:

(a) encode the 10 hand-traced bindings into the resolver (module-level accessors returning the runtime, object-literal factory captures, structural inline parameter types, dependency-object ports), and resolve the own-class callback case by doctrine; or
(b) declare the hand-triage part of the manifest rather than of the machine authority, which means the authority is not fully automated and the manifest becomes load-bearing
Re-derive the status/classification from the corrected authority, which moves TX_BOUNDARY 100 -> 83 and TEST_ONLY_OR_DEAD 13 -> 14, and produces the 16 REVIEW_REQUIRED that must be closed first

Re-run the audit baselines that currently pin TX_BOUNDARY: 100 / TEST_ONLY_OR_DEAD: 13 (scripts/ts6-audit/c2r15-authority-correction.test.ts:48-54, scripts/ts6-audit/regression-evidence-authority.test.ts:33-39)
Re-verify the 112 relations: 5 boundaries lose PROVEN, so they leave the coverage-required set; no relation proof is invalidated
explicitNonClaims: No callersFor change has been applied.
No fixture, frozen artifact, or inventory value has been changed.
golden.v5 remains valid as the corrected regression-evidence projection.
The 94 figure is NOT an authority output and must not be adopted as the target.
recommendation: Proceed with A′ but gate it on closing the REVIEW_REQUIRED class to zero, because the validator rejects any projection that contains one. Recommended order: (1) treat recoverExpiredLeases as its own decision — doctrine question, not code discovery; (2) encode the 10 hand-traced bindings into the resolver; (3) confirm the 5 collisions; (4) only then re-derive the corrected projection and update the audit baselines. Attempting the derivation before step 2 produces a projection the tool rejects, which is why the current 94/18/1 cannot be the target.
